prerequisites: Students are expected to have a solid knowledge of procedural and object-oriented programming and to be familiar with relational database systems.

They should be able to design and implement software applications using appropriate algorithms, data structures, and object-oriented programming techniques, as well as interact with databases and network services.
Basic knowledge of operating systems and integrated development environments (IDEs) is also beneficial.

learning_outcomes.text: understand the main phases of the software development process
model software requirements, structure, and behavior using UML
apply established software design principles and design patterns
employ agile methodologies for software development
plan and perform software verification and validation activities
develop software collaboratively using version control and team collaboration tools
understand the principles underlying modern cloud platforms and DevOps practices

Upon successful completion of the course, students will have acquired knowledge of the fundamental principles of Software Engineering, the main software development process models, object-oriented analysis and design methodologies, software verification and validation techniques, software quality principles, and the technologies and practices underpinning contemporary software development.

Students will be able to analyze software requirements, model software systems using UML, design object-oriented software architectures and components, apply established design principles and design patterns, employ agile software development methodologies, carry out software testing activities, and use software configuration management and collaborative development tools within a software project.

Students will be able to critically evaluate alternative software design and architectural solutions, selecting appropriate methods, tools, and techniques according to system requirements, project constraints, and quality objectives. They will also be able to assess software quality aspects and critically appreciate the opportunities and limitations of modern software engineering technologies, including Artificial Intelligence-based software development tools.

Students will be able to effectively document software analysis, design, implementation, and testing activities using appropriate models, diagrams, and technical documentation. They will also be able to communicate and justify design decisions, present project outcomes, and collaborate effectively within a software development team using appropriate technical terminology.

Students will develop the ability to independently deepen their knowledge of emerging software engineering methodologies, technologies, and tools, enabling them to adapt to the continuous evolution of software development practices and to pursue further studies in the field.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Software Engineering: Software as an engineered product; Evolution of Software Engineering; Software lifecycle; Software quality attributes; Software cost and complexity
Software Development Processes: Waterfall model; Incremental process; Iterative process; Unified Process; Risk-driven processes; Comparison of software development processes
Agile Methods: Agile Manifesto; XP; Scrum; User Stories; Sprint Planning; Product Backlog; Continuous Feedback; Introduction to Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery
Software Configuration Management: Version control; Git and distributed repositories; Branching and merging; Code review; Build automation; Release management
Requirements Engineering: Functional and non-functional requirements; Requirements elicitation techniques; Requirements specification; Use Cases; User Stories; Requirements traceability
UML: Introduction to the Unified Modeling Language (UML); main UML diagrams
Software Design: Principles of object-oriented design; Encapsulation; Abstraction; Inheritance; Polymorphism; Cohesion and coupling; Responsibility assignment; Introduction to the SOLID principles

Software Architecture: Software architecture; Architectural patterns; Layered architecture; Model-View-Controller (MVC); Client-Server architecture; Service-oriented architectures; Introduction to microservices
Design Patterns: Motivation; Creational patterns; Structural patterns; Behavioral patterns; Practical applications of the main Gang of Four (GoF) design patterns
Software Quality: Software quality attributes; Technical debt; Refactoring; Maintainability; Software metrics

Software Testing: Verification and validation; Software testing; Testing levels; Unit testing; Integration testing; System testing; Acceptance testing; Black-box and white-box testing; Test case design; Code coverage; Test automation; Unit testing frameworks

Technologies and Practices for Contemporary Software Development: Software as a Service (SaaS); Cloud Computing; Introduction to DevOps; Continuous Deployment; Containerization (overview); Introduction to the use of Artificial Intelligence as a support tool for software development (AI-assisted software development)

Laboratory activities including requirements analysis; UML modeling; architectural design; implementation; use of version control systems; application of Agile practices; development of automated tests; project documentation; final presentation.

assessment_methods.method: Group project, including requirements analysis, software design, implementation, testing, and documentation, with a final presentation and discussion

assessment_rules: Assessment will consider not only the technical correctness of the proposed solutions but also the quality of the software design, the documentation produced, teamwork skills, and the clarity of the presentation.
